parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, border rule, facility rule or custody rule is documented: same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 1991 and police/military/prison were stated (1998) not to discriminate on sexual orientation. Against that, the outed visitor faces documented societal hostility with thin recourse: a 2017 carnival assault on a gay visitor, nine unsolved murders of gay men (2001–2015), jury and Court of Appeal tolerance of gay-panic force, no hate-crime or anti-discrimination law, constitutional exclusion of gender identity, and a government member publicly demanding 'Exile of Transgender.' The scene is underground. Border screening and trans-specific data are absent — uncertainty, not safety. Worst feature is tier 3 hostility with no working remedy, no tier-1 state exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: No source covers border screening, document-marker rules, visa treatment or secondary inspection for trans travellers; mismatch friction is an open question, not a documented rule.
entry_documents.protection: No trans-specific entry restriction, criminal offence or registration requirement is documented; same-sex conduct decriminalised 1991.
entry_documents.interaction: Any document mismatch would meet a conservative social climate and thin recourse rather than a stated border policy.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No national hate-crime law; juries acquitted/leniently sentenced killers using gay-panic defences (2009 acquittal; 10 June 2010 Court of Appeal remark endorsing force); nine unsolved murders of gay men 2001–2015.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 1998 ministerial statement that police, military and prison service do not discriminate on sexual orientation; 2007 capital party raid produced no arrests and a Ministry of Tourism apology.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If a trans visitor is assaulted or detained, no bias-charge mechanism exists and courts have excused anti-LGBT force; no trans-specific detention record exists either way.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No standing subnational variation documented; whether conditions differ outside the capital is unmeasured.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Capital nightlife raid history shows tourism-facing authorities distancing from anti-LGBT policing, but no trans-specific facility protection exists.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National findings (unsolved murders, legal gaps) apply countrywide regardless of locality.

care_services.exposure: Gender-identity discrimination in healthcare is not illegal; no HIV-specific or trans-specific care provisions recorded; gender-affirming care availability unknown — an emergency could out a visitor to staff facing no duty to treat.
care_services.interaction: Injury or illness converts outing probability into a service-denial exposure with no recorded remedy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: A government member publicly demanded 'Exile of Transgender out of the country,' pledging $1,000; former head of government defined marriage by birth sex; 2006 constitutional reform excluded sexual orientation and gender identity on religious grounds; 2016 referendum bills excluded trans/intersex people.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Communications Act 2009 empowers the regulator to code against inciting hatred on sexual preference; 1998 non-discrimination statement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official rhetoric licenses social hostility and weakens any complaint a visitor might make, while remaining rhetoric rather than operative policy.

minors_guardians.exposure: Unequal age of consent: 16 opposite-sex, 18 same-sex, with life imprisonment recorded for sex with a same-sex minor — a relationship read as same-sex involving a 16–17-year-old is a documented criminal exposure. Custody or family treatment of an accompanying minor is not covered.
minors_guardians.protection: None documented specific to travelling families.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans parent's family read as same-sex could attract both social hostility and this higher threshold; no custody rule is recorded.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 8 May 2017: gay visitor hospitalised with head laceration, 'targeted and beaten,' at the national carnival, seeking charges (outcome unresolved); no hate-crime law to charge bias; LGBT tourist groups protested (1998, 2004, 2007); 85.5% strongly disapproving same-sex marriage (2015); scene underground; 2005 beauty queen stripped of title.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Police officially non-discriminatory (1998); Ministry of Tourism apology after 2007 raid; ordinary assault law theoretically available.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: The visitor assaulted in a crowd faces a society with documented disapproval, no bias-charge tool, and courts that have excused anti-LGBT force.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination statute covering gender identity, Constitution excludes it, no hate-crime law, judicial tolerance of gay-panic defences, and pressure to keep LGBT events hidden — recourse is thin.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Data Protection Act 2003 lists 'sexual life' as sensitive personal data; Communications Act anti-incitement code; ordinary criminal and civil remedies formally available.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unknowns remain on border screening, care access, trans-specific attitudes, and whether 2017 charges were laid; absence of evidence is not safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's Visitor Conduct Register is a universal, state-enforced entry bar with no remedy — tier 1. This dossier documents no entry exclusion, registration, detention or facility rule against visitors at all, so it sits materially above 0.35-A; the offsetting features (official exile rhetoric, violence with judicial tolerance) are hostility and impunity rather than state machinery.

Kestrel Isles' discretionary secondary screening and refusal of entry is a documented, recurring administrative exposure affecting many arrivals. Here the border axis is simply undocumented while the documented axis is physical violence excused by courts and no bias-charge remedy — rarer but more severe, with no recorded screening harm. Slightly below 0.55-B on combined frequency-weighted exposure.

Vellmaris shows a document-mismatch stop cured by national equality law, advocacy intervention, apology and compensation. This dossier has no equality law covering gender identity, no working remedy, and courts endorsing anti-LGBT force — so materially below 0.65-A, where functioning protections absorbed an isolated incident.

Drellia's mandatory address registration and nightly hotel transmission is a universal-exposure measure forcing routine disclosure. Nothing comparable is documented here — no registration, database or marker-disclosure rule reaches this visitor — which lifts the rating above 0.45-D despite comparable official and social hostility.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a hostile society with a passive-to-tolerant state, not an active persecuting one: no trans-specific offence, entry rule, facility rule or custody rule is documented, and same-sex conduct has been lawful since 1991. What follows discovery is instead social hostility backed by thin recourse — a visitor was hospitalised after being beaten at carnival in 2017, bias charges have no statutory basis, courts have excused anti-LGBT force, nine murders of gay men went unsolved, a government member demanded exile of transgender people, and constitutional and statutory law exclude gender identity entirely. Border, care and trans-specific data are missing, so uncertainty is not credited as safety. For an adult with a minor, the unequal age of consent (18 for same-sex acts, life imprisonment for a same-sex minor) adds a latent criminal exposure with no documented custody protections.
